newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas trade limited to 6 deals as prices rise.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas trade limited to 6 deals as prices rise.

text.p: The IPE natural gas futures market closed on Friday afternoon with a total of 105 lots traded in only six separate trades, to end a disappointing week in terms of volume.
There were 20 lots traded on Monday, 110 on Tuesday, 205 on Wednesday and 190 on Thursday, so there was no one day on which the market really took off.

Trade on Friday was done on our different months spread across the curve, with no concentration on a single period as there had been on Thursday when there was a focus on the winter. But prices were up across the board, with October seeing the biggest rise, by 0.275 pence a therm to settle at 12.55 pence.

This has widened the contango at the beginning of next winter to 1.95 pence a therm between September and October, considerably steeper than the contango between October and November or November and December.
But despite the trading opportunities which this could present, trade remained stubbornly subdued.
